# docs.langchain.com documentation — Langsmith — Overview — Part 121

> 60 page(s) of docs.langchain.com documentation — Langsmith — Overview under Part 121. Part of the index one level up (../llms.txt).

## Part 121

- [Double texting](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/double-texting.md): This option allows the current run to finish before processing any new input. Incoming requests are queued and executed sequentially once prior runs complete.
- [Add encryption at rest](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/encryption.md): Agent Server supports encryption at rest for checkpoint data and metadata. You can choose between basic encryption with a single key or custom encryption for advanced use cases.
- [API and SDK deprecation policy](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/endpoint-deprecation.md): LangSmith deprecates API endpoints and SDK methods before removing them, so you have time to migrate to a replacement.
- [Connect LangSmith Engine to GitHub](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-github.md): Connecting a GitHub repository is optional. When connected, LangSmith Engine reads source code to diagnose issues and opens pull requests with proposed fixes.
- [LangSmith Engine issue categories](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-issue-categories.md): When [LangSmith Engine](/langsmith/engine) detects a recurring issue in your traces, it tags the issue with a category.
- [LangSmith Engine](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-overview.md): LangSmith Engine is the LangSmith Agent for agent engineering.
- [LangSmith Engine security](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security.md): LangSmith Engine is an AI agent built into LangSmith that improves the agents you build.
- [LangSmith Engine on Self-hosted](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-self-hosted.md): Self-hosted Engine requires LangSmith Helm chart `0.16.0` or later and a license that includes the Engine entitlement. It is not available on earlier chart versions.
- [LangSmith Engine webhook events](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-webhooks.md): Forward LangSmith-detected agent issues into your incident-management, paging, or chat tools.
- [Find and fix your agent's issues with LangSmith Engine](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine.md): LangSmith Engine helps you ship more reliable agents without manually searching through traces.
- [Enqueue concurrent](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/enqueue-concurrent.md): This guide assumes knowledge of what double-texting is, which you can learn about in the [double-texting conceptual guide](/langsmith/double-texting).
- [Cloud Agent Server environment variables](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-cloud.md): The Agent Server supports the following environment variables when deployed on [Cloud](/langsmith/deploy-to-cloud-overview).
- [Self-hosted Agent Server environment variables](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/env-var-self-hosted.md): The Agent Server supports the following environment variables when deployed on [self-hosted](/langsmith/deploy-to-self-hosted-overview) infrastructure.
- [Evaluate a chatbot](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-chatbot-tutorial.md): In this guide we will set up evaluations for a chatbot. These allow you to measure how well your application is performing over a set of data.
- [Evaluate a complex agent](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-complex-agent.md): In this tutorial, we'll build a customer support bot that helps users navigate a digital music store.
- [How to add evaluators to an existing experiment (Python only)](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-existing-experiment.md): Evaluation of existing experiments is currently only supported in the Python SDK.
- [How to evaluate a graph](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-graph.md): `langgraph` is a library for building stateful, multi-actor applications with LLMs, used to create agent and multi-agent workflows.
- [How to evaluate agents](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-llm-application.md): This guide shows you how to run an evaluation on an agent using the LangSmith SDK.
- [How to evaluate an application's intermediate steps](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluate-on-intermediate-steps.md): While, in many scenarios, it is sufficient to evaluate the final output of your task, in some cases you might want to evaluate the intermediate steps of your pipeline.

- [Evaluation concepts](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts.md): LLM outputs are non-deterministic, which makes response quality hard to assess. Evaluations (evals) are a way to breakdown what "good" looks like and measure it.

- [Track and limit evaluator spend](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluator-spend.md): Cap weekly LLM spend per evaluator to prevent a single evaluator from exceeding your budget. LangSmith tracks week-to-date evaluator spend, resetting at Monday 12AM UTC.
